Simultaneously, an internal hook or shuttle catches this upper thread and wraps it around the rotating **bobbin**. This action pulls the bobbin thread through the same path. When the machine completes a stitch cycle, the two threads interlock beneath the surface of the material, forming a secure, continuous seam that holds the fabric together effectively.

A thermostat operates by continuously monitoring the ambient temperature within a controlled space. When the actual room temperature drops below this established lower threshold—indicating it's too cool—the thermostat interprets this difference as a need for heating. This discrepancy triggers an electrical signal, sending power to the HVAC system's furnace or heater. Conversely, if the temperature rises above the upper threshold, signaling sufficient warmth, the circuit opens, shutting the heating element off until the cooling effect causes another drop below the set point again.
